key_insight: Boundary-layer detachment and breakdown of Prandtl scaling can coexist with numerical convergence toward a smooth Euler flow as Reynolds number increases.
engineering_relevance: The results caution against treating boundary-layer detachment alone as evidence that an inviscid model cannot approximate bulk flow in the energy norm.
method: Run highly resolved direct numerical simulations in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls.
Construct Reynolds-dependent initial conditions with Prandtl-thickness boundary layers approaching a stationary analytic Euler flow.
Track velocity-error energy, dissipation, and detached-vortex behavior as Reynolds number increases.
evidence_signal: Over the simulated time interval, both the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and time-averaged energy dissipation scale approximately as Re^(-1/2), supporting convergence despite detachment.
watch_item: The evidence is numerical and limited to the studied two-dimensional setup and simulated time interval; it does not establish general or long-time convergence.
paper_title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
